newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Precooked president to be challenged.
newsitem.headline: Precooked president to be challenged.

text.p: The man chosen by the European Parliament's two biggest groups to become president next Tuesday is being challenged by former Council of Europe Secretary General Catherine Lalumiere.

Under a longstanding deal between the Socialists and the European People's Party, the election of Spanish EPP deputy Jose-Maria Gil-Robles has been precooked and is a certainty next Tuesday in Strasbourg.
The two groups share the presidency during the parliament's five-year term.

Lalumiere, a former French European Affairs Minister and leader of the parliament's alternative European Radical Alliance group, threw her hat into the ring in protest at what smaller groups see as the undemocratic way of selecting the president.
"This procedure excludes the smaller EU member states and the small parliamentary groups," she said in a statement.
Although she has no real chance of being elected, parliamentary officials said she could well clock up around 100 of the parliament's 626 votes as many deputies from the smaller groups will back her.

"She is more than a symbolic candidate," German leader of the Greens Claudia Roth told Reuters, saying Lalumiere had European experience and that "after years and years and years of men it would be a good thing to have a woman."
"All the arguments are for her," she said.
The president of the parliament's Liberal Group, Gijs De Vries, a Dutchman, said his group would back Lalumiere.
"It demonstrates our deep dissatisfaction at the undemocratic procedure used by the socialists and Christian Democrats," he told Reuters.
